title: Longest no-repeat stretch
prompt:
A playlist is encoded as a string where each character is one track; return the length of the longest contiguous stretch in which no track character repeats.

- playlist has 0 to 50,000 printable ASCII characters (letters, digits, symbols, spaces); characters are case-sensitive.
- Return an integer (0 for an empty string).

hints: Checking every substring is O(n^2) or worse. If a window has no repeats, so does every window inside it.
Grow a window to the right one character at a time; when the new character already appears in the window, move the left edge past its earlier copy.
Store the last index of each character. On character c at index r, set left = max(left, last[c] + 1), then last[c] = r and best = max(best, r - left + 1).

solution.explanation: The window [left, r] always holds distinct characters. A repeat of c forces left past c's previous index; the max() keeps left from moving backwards when that previous index is already outside the window. Both edges only move right, so the scan is linear.

complexity.notes: The map holds at most one entry per distinct character.

followUps: Return the stretch itself, choosing the leftmost one on ties.
Allow each character to appear at most twice in the window.
